ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Identical code with W_i = I_d for every item (no successor second moment, no alpha, no eigenbasis); everything else, including Mobius prefix composition and the Poincare chord, unchanged. The switch exists and is exercised only by unit tests in this round, not trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run: successor-frame warp W_i inside the warped Poincare chord with Mobius prefix composition, trained once, no sweep, no extra seed, no early stopping.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Identical code with the curved terms replaced: chord measured in flat coordinates, d = || W_i( z_i - (p_{l-1} + u_{l,k}) ) ||^2, prefix composed by plain vector addition; the behaviour warp W_i stays. Switch exists, not trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: Adjacent pairs (item_t, item_{t+1}) counted over all training-split user sequences only, aggregated into a sparse 24556 x 24556 count matrix A; pi_ij normalised over the smallest successor set covering 0.8 of each item's outgoing mass; successors projected through the current detached encoder to tangent coordinates t_j at the origin. Recomputed once per epoch, no gradient.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item transitions: the per-item successor distribution over training sequences.
ideas.cost_estimate: +10-20% Stage-2 epoch time at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs). Per step: 1023 items x 3 levels x 256 codewords x one d x d matvec (d=32) ~ 0.86 GFLOP forward, ~2.5 GFLOP with backward, versus ~0.05 GFLOP for the baseline assignment; assignment is a small share of the encoder step. One batched 24556-way 32x32 eigh per epoch (~30 ms GPU) plus a sparse successor gather, <= ~5 min over the whole of Stage 2. Stage-3 cost unchanged.
ideas.coupling_equation: d_{l,i,k} = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( sqrt(c) * || W_i [ (-z_i) (+) ( p_{l-1,i} (+) u_{l,k} ) ] || ), with W_i = B_i diag(s_i) B_i^T, M_i = sum_{j in S_i} pi_ij t_j t_j^T = B_i diag(lambda) B_i^T, s_i,k = exp(0.5 * alpha_i * (log lambda_k - mean log lambda)), alpha_i = lambda_1 / sum lambda; behaviour enters through pi_ij and alpha_i, curvature through (+), (-) and artanh, and both meet inside the same norm that selects the codeword.
ideas.coupling_path: One pathway: training successor distribution -> successor second moment in the ball's tangent space -> det-1 warp W_i -> warped Poincare chord -> nearest-codeword index at level l -> level-l SID token -> Mobius composition of the prefix -> loss gradient on encoder and codebooks -> next epoch's frames. Removing behaviour sets W_i = I and the pathway collapses to plain hyperbolic RQ; removing geometry replaces the warped Poincare chord with a warped Euclidean chord and Mobius prefix with plain addition, so neither term can be dropped without changing the selection that produces the SID.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If successor structure in the training transition graph predicts next-item and the successor directions in the Poincare ball are not the content-reconstruction directions, the single coupled run gives Stage-3 test Recall@10 > 0.065, and training transition pairs (i->j) share level-1 and level-2 prefixes at a higher rate than the same frozen encoder's codes produce under the identity frame (post-hoc re-assignment, no extra training). If Recall lands at or below the identity-frame expectation, the successor second moment is not the right frame and the idea is dropped.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE residual quantizer of Stage 2, at every level l = 1..L: codeword selection, the per-level reconstruction/commitment term, and the prefix composition p_l = p_{l-1} (+) u_{l,k_l}. Not in the item encoder and not in Stage 3.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative-curvature Poincare ball with c = 1 (unit ball, r_max = 1 - 1e-3): exp/log maps at the origin, Mobius addition (+) and subtraction, hyperbolic distance (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||.||), and a determinant-one linear warp W_i applied to the chord before the artanh. Curvature is fixed, not trainable.
ideas.key_change: Every level's nearest-codeword rule and every level's reconstruction/commitment term use the warped Poincare distance d^W(z, p_{l-1} (+) u) = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c) * || W_i ( (-z) (+) (p_{l-1} (+) u) ) ||) with W_i = B_i diag(s_i) B_i^T taken from the eigendecomposition of the item's successor second moment M_i = sum_j pi_ij t_j t_j^T, while the prefix itself is composed by Mobius addition p_l = p_{l-1} (+) u_{l,k_l}.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Transitions and successor sets come only from the Stage-2 training split over the 24556 training items; validation and test interactions are never read, so no validation/test user contributes an edge and no validation/test item can appear as a successor. The SID table is frozen before Stage 3, and Stage 3 trains and is evaluated without any further SID update, so no test statistic can re-enter code construction; the identity-frame diagnostic uses only training transition pairs.
ideas.motivation: The RQ-VAE spends SID prefix resolution in directions that are convenient for item-content reconstruction, not in the directions in which users actually move. For a generative recommender this is a direct loss: two items a user routinely moves between can land in different level-1 or level-2 prefixes, so the generator cannot condition the next prefix on the current one. The defect is not where the codewords sit but the metric in which each level measures its residual.
ideas.novelty: Codeword parameters, codebook initialisation, codebook updates and curvature are left exactly as in the baseline; what changes is the metric of the residual quantizer. Each item gets a determinant-one linear reparametrisation W_i of the hyperbolic chord, built from its training successor second moment in the ball's tangent space at the origin, and the same W_i is applied at every level so it shapes the whole prefix hierarchy at once. Earlier mechanisms here re-positioned codewords (Fréchet/Karcher/mass-weighted), set a per-level curvature (CURVCTRL), set radial position from transition entropy (BRad), smoothed successor profiles in Lorentz coordinates, or imposed behaviour cones; none warps the curved distance that selects codewords, and none derives warp strength from the dominant eigenvalue share of the successor second moment.
ideas.observables: Per-level codeword usage histograms and number of used codewords; the distribution of alpha_i and of s_max/s_min; successor prefix-agreement rate at level 1 and level 2 over training transition pairs for the trained SID versus the same encoder under the identity frame; prefix-transition predictability of the generator (accuracy of predicting the next item's level-l token from the current item's level-l prefix); Stage-3 test Recall@10 against the 0.065 bar; the gradient norm the warped term contributes to the encoder.

rejected_ideas.reason: out of scope: ablation_geometry_off does not say what replaces the curve

risks: alpha_i times the eigenvalue spread may over-concentrate prefix resolution into a few successor directions and damage reconstruction, so codes stop covering the catalogue; 0.8-mass successor sets can be tiny (1-2 items) and noisy for tail items, giving near-degenerate frames; per-epoch frame refresh makes the metric non-stationary, which can stop the codebooks from settling; warping the chord can push ||q|| toward 1, where artanh gradients explode; successor information may already be captured by Stage 3's sequence model, leaving only reconstruction damage; computing a second identity-frame assignment for the diagnostic adds a code path that could silently diverge from the trained one
ideas.safeguards: Mobius arithmetic in the algebraically stable form with denominator floored at 1e-8; every achieved point re-projected to ||p|| <= r_max = 1-1e-3 after each addition and each codebook update; chord rescaled if the warp pushes it past r_max; artanh argument clipped to 1-1e-7 and implemented as 0.5*log((1+x)/(1-x)); eigenvalue floor relative to the measured trace; s_i clipped to [1/sqrt(d), sqrt(d)] so det(W)=1 and no direction is annihilated; alpha_i clipped to [0,1]; frames detached and refreshed only once per epoch; identity fallback for items with fewer than two successors or zero outgoing mass; the identity-frame diagnostic re-uses the same distance function object as the trained path; NaN/Inf guard on the per-level loss with the step skipped and logged if triggered.
ideas.spec_equations: epoch hook (no grad):   A <- transitions(training sequences); t_i <- log_0^c(z_i) with z_i = exp_0^c(clip(f(e_i), R)), detached   for each i: S_i <- min set covering 0.8 * out_mass(i); pi_i <- normalise(A_i,S_i)      M_i <- sum_{j in S_i} pi_ij t_j t_j^T ; (lambda, B_i) <- eigh_desc(M_i)      lambda <- max(lambda, 1e-6*mean(lambda)+1e-12); alpha_i <- lambda_1/sum(lambda)      s_i <- clip( exp( 0.5*alpha_i*(log lambda - mean(log lambda)) ), 1/sqrt(d), sqrt(d) )      W_i <- B_i diag(s_i) B_i^T          # det = 1   fallback: |S_i| < 2 or out_mass(i)=0 -> W_i <- I_d step hook (levels l = 1..L):   p_0 <- 0   ch_{i,k} <- mobius_add( mobius_neg(z_i), mobius_add(p_{l-1,i}, u_{l,k}) )   q_{i,k} <- W_i ch_{i,k};  q <- q * min(1, r_max/(||q||+1e-12))   d_{i,k} <- (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh( sqrt(c)*||q_{i,k}|| )   # arg clipped to 1-1e-7   k_l <- argmin_k d ; token_l <- k_l ; p_{l,i} <- clip_ball( mobius_add(p_{l-1,i}, u_{l,k_l}), r_max )   loss <- sum_l d_{i,k_l}^2 + beta * commitment(...)  # beta = baseline value   straight-through gradient from p_{l,i} to encoder latent; W_i detached
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs per item: content embedding e_i, prefix point p_{l-1,i} in the ball, level-l codebook U_l inside the ball, and the precomputed frame (B_i, s_i) i.e. W_i. Outputs per item per level: chosen index k_l and hence the level-l SID token, the new prefix point p_{l,i} in the ball, and the scalar warped Poincare distance used in the loss. Episode-level output: the SID table (item -> (token_1,...,token_L)) consumed by Stage 3, plus recorded frames and distances.

specification.text: (1) Offline, once per Stage-2 epoch, no gradient: A = directed adjacent-transition counts over training sequences only (item at t -> item at t+1), 24556 x 24556 sparse; z = exp_0^c(clip(E_content, ||.|| <= R)) from the current encoder, detached; t = log_0^c(z). Per item i: S_i = smallest successor set covering >= 0.8 of i's outgoing transition mass; pi_ij = A_ij / sum_{j in S_i} A_ij; if |S_i| < 2 or mass 0 then B_i = I_d, s_i = 1. Else M_i = sum_{j in S_i} pi_ij t_j t_j^T (uncentred, so mean successor direction and spread both enter), eigh -> lambda descending, B_i; lambda <- max(lambda, 1e-6*mean(lambda)+1e-12); alpha_i = lambda_1/sum_k lambda_k; s_i = exp(0.5*alpha_i*(log lambda - mean_k log lambda)) clipped to [1/sqrt(d), sqrt(d)]; W_i = B_i diag(s_i) B_i^T (det = 1). (2) Quantization, levels l = 1..L: p_0 = 0; ch_k = (-z_i) (+) (p_{l-1} (+) u_{l,k}); q_k = W_i ch_k, rescaled to r_max if longer; d_{l,i,k} = (2/sqrt(c)) artanh(sqrt(c)||q_k||); k_l = argmin_k d (straight-through); p_l = clip_ball(p_{l-1} (+) u_{l,k_l}). (3) Loss = sum_l d_{l,i,k_l}^2 + beta * commitment with beta and codebook/EMA settings exactly the baseline's (no new loss constant); codebook entries projected into the ball to radius <= 0.9 after each step; W_i detached.

ideas.title: Successor-frame warped Poincare quantization: one determinant-one behaviour metric shared by every RQ level

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: beta_i set to 0 for every item, everything else identical, so the cost degenerates to the plain isotropic Poincare distance; implemented behind a config flag and NOT trained this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full mechanism as specified (behaviour-derived beta_i and u_i plus curvature c = 1 Mobius gauge in both assignment and codebook update); this is the single trained run of the round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Take the c -> 0 flat limit: (-r)(+)w becomes plain subtraction, 2*artanh(sqrt(c*q))/sqrt(c) becomes 2*sqrt(||x-y||^2 + beta*<x-y,uhat>^2), and the Frechet update becomes a plain mean; implemented behind a config flag and NOT trained this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From Stage-2 training sequences only, count directed co-occurrences N_ij inside the training window and row-normalise to p_ij = N_ij / sum_j N_ij. With z_j = log0(exp0(.) ) of the item input embedding, b_i = sum_j p_ij * z_j/||z_j||, beta_i = ||b_i|| which lies in [0,1] by convexity of unit vectors, u_i = b_i/||b_i||. Recomputed once per epoch from the current embeddings and frozen within the epoch; items with no training successors get beta_i = 0 and u_i = 0.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions from the training split only, summarised per item as a successor resultant direction u_i and a successor concentration beta_i.
ideas.cost_estimate: No new parameters, no tuned constants. +1 dot product per (item, level, code) triple: about +30% on the level-wise distance kernel and under 5% wall clock. Per step at the frozen scale (batch B items x L levels x K codes x d dims; e.g. B=1024, L=4, K=256, d=64) that is ~6.7e7 extra multiply-adds for the anisotropic term; 24 steps/epoch and 3000 epochs unchanged. Behaviour refresh costs |E| x d (~5e5 x 64 = 3.2e7 multiply-adds) once per epoch, under 1% of an epoch. Sparse transition matmul, so memory is negligible.
ideas.coupling_equation: d_{i,k}^{(l)} = 2*artanh( sqrt( ||(-r_l)(+)w_k||_{c}^2 + beta_i * < (-r_l)(+)w_k , uhat_l >^2 ) ), with beta_i = || sum_j p_ij * zhat_j || (behaviour term) and the Mobius addition and artanh with curvature c = 1 (curved terms).
ideas.coupling_path: Training transitions -> (beta_i, u_i) -> the anisotropic curved cost that selects the code at level l -> the assigned residual whose tangent mean becomes codebook entry w_k at level l -> the level-(l+1) base point -> the emitted SID. Setting beta=0 removes the behaviour term from that same cost; flattening c removes the Mobius/artanh structure from that same cost; either change alters which code is chosen, hence the codebooks and the SIDs.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the gauge is doing hierarchical work, then with the switches on the level-1 prefix hit rate of training transitions and the RQ reconstruction at level 1 both improve and the single Stage-3 run gives test_recall@10 above 0.065; if recall does not move while the prefix hit rate does, the gain is not reaching the generative model and the idea is dropped.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the residual quantiser of every RQ level: both in the assignment step (distance from residual to code) and in the codebook update (tangent-space Frechet mean of the assigned residuals), i.e. in the SID construction itself rather than in an auxiliary loss.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c = 1: Mobius addition (+), tanh/artanh exponential and logarithmic maps at the origin, Poincare distance d(x,y) = 2*artanh||(-x)(+)y||, extended by the anisotropic gauge q(delta) = ||delta||^2 + beta*<delta,uhat>^2 and d_aniso = 2*artanh(sqrt(q)).
ideas.key_change: Residual quantisation runs in the unit Poincare ball with Mobius residuals and a per-item anisotropic gauge (stretch 1+beta_i along u_i), so along-successor mismatches cost more than orthogonal ones; assignment uses that cost and codebooks are updated as tangent Frechet means of the resulting assigned residuals.
ideas.leakage_boundary: N_ij is built exclusively from Stage-2 training-split sequences before Stage 3 starts; item ids are frozen up front and no validation or test interaction is read at any point. The behaviour table is a periodic re-read of training counts only, so no validation or test item, transition or co-consumption can enter the SID construction.
ideas.motivation: In a plain Euclidean RQ-VAE the level-1 code of an item is a generic residual direction; items that are behaviourally interchangeable as predecessors (their training successors point the same way) are not pushed to share a coarse prefix, so the generative model must spend prefix capacity on behaviour-irrelevant geometry.
ideas.novelty: Prior rounds moved codebook placement (Frechet/successor means), curvature schedules, radial ranking, cone/prefix boosting and successor-profile smoothing. This changes the metric itself: each item carries its own anisotropic Poincare gauge whose stretch axis is the training successor direction and whose stretch magnitude is the measured successor concentration, applied inside the same closed-form distance that drives assignment and codebook update.
ideas.observables: Per-level code assignment histograms and codebook usage; level-1 and level-2 prefix hit rate of training transitions and prefix counts (diagnostics, recorded not gated); SID drift for items with coherent versus diffuse successor fields; per-level RQ reconstruction error; Stage-3 test_recall@10 as the sole judgement.
risks: Anisotropy may be too mild: beta in [0,1] bounds the stretch at sqrt(2), so codes may barely move.; Successor direction is noisy for tail items with few training transitions, so beta is small exactly where it could help.; Mobius residuals plus Frechet codebook updates are harder to optimise and may collapse codebook usage.; The once-per-epoch behaviour refresh lags embedding drift and could inject stale directions.; Single run, single seed: the effect may be inside seed noise and the programme cannot repeat it.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp ||x|| to at most 1-1e-5 before log0 and before artanh; clamp the artanh argument to 1-1e-6 and use a finite-gradient safe artanh; clamp the Mobius denominator (1+2<a,b>+||a||^2||b||^2) to at least 1e-8; guarantee beta in [0,1] by construction (mean of unit vectors) and set beta=0, u=0 when ||b_i||<1e-8 (cold or unseen items); nan_to_num on the Frechet mean and freeze any code that received no assignment instead of moving it; cast the transition counts to the model dtype and keep the diameter term in float32 for the sparse refresh.
ideas.spec_equations: exp0(v) = tanh(||v||) * v/||v||; log0(x) = artanh(||x||) * x/||x||; a(+)b = ((1+2<a,b>+||b||^2)a + (1-||a||^2)b) / (1+2<a,b>+||a||^2||b||^2). p_0 = 0; for l = 1..L: r = (-p)(+)x; for k: delta_k = (-r)(+)w_k; q_k = ||delta_k||^2 + beta_i*<delta_k,uhat_l>^2; d_k = 2*artanh(min(sqrt(q_k), 1-1e-6)); k* = argmin_k d_k; p = p(+)w_{k*}; SID_i[l] = k*. Update: w_k <- exp0( sum_{i assigned to k} log0(r_i) / count_k ). Behaviour: p_ij = N_ij/sum_j N_ij, b_i = sum_j p_ij zhat_j, beta_i = ||b_i||, u_i = b_i/||b_i||, uhat_l = normalise(log0(exp0(u_i)(-)p_l)).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: item embedding z_i from the RQ-VAE encoder, the per-item training transition table giving (beta_i, u_i), the current level codebooks as ball points, and the current level base point p_l. Outputs: per-level code indices forming the SID, the quantised ball point p_L, updated codebooks, and the standard reconstruction and commitment losses computed in the tangent space at the origin.

specification.text: c=1 fixed (tanh/artanh chart, scale-free, no normalisation constant). Per item i from training transitions obtain beta_i in [0,1] and unit tangent direction u_i; if the item has no training successors set beta_i=0. At each RQ level l, with base point p_l in the ball and target x_i=exp0(z_i): r_l = (-p_l) (+) x_i; for every code w_k compute d_k = 2*artanh(sqrt(||(-r_l)(+)w_k||^2 + beta_i*<(-r_l)(+)w_k, uhat_l>^2)) with uhat_l = normalise(log0(exp0(u_i) (-) p_l)); assign k* = argmin_k d_k; carry p_{l+1} = p_l (+) w_{k*}. Codebook update: w_k <- exp0(mean over assigned items of log0(r_l)). Behaviour table refreshed once per epoch from the current item embeddings. Three switches exist in code: behaviour off (beta=0), geometry off (c->0 flat limit), both on (the single trained run).

ideas.title: Behaviour-anisotropic Poincare gauge metric for RQ-VAE residual assignment and codebook update

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: tau_l = 0 for all levels: the cost is the pure Poincare-distance assignment, with the successor distribution computed but never entering the argmin.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run, geodesic distance plus successor-code margin, which is the single arm actually trained.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: d_P^2 replaced by ||z_i^(l-1) - e_lk||^2 with no exp_0/log_0 maps and no curvature, same margin: a Euclidean margin-shifted RQ assignment.
ideas.behavior_computation: One pass over the training split's sequences only: for each adjacent pair (s_u[t], s_u[t+1]) increment c_ij; then w_ij = c_ij/sqrt(1+c_j) with c_j the in-degree, p_ij = w_ij/sum_j' w_ij, and keep the top-10 successors per item (documented default) as a frozen sparse CSR block. At each training step the successor codes are read from a detached integer cache h_l over all 24556 items, refreshed only with the hard assignments of the current batch after the step.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions (the successor profile) from the training user sequences, popularity-adjusted, restricted to the Stage-2 item set; no self-transitions and no repeated users within a pair.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch, batch about 1023, K_l = 256, d = 64, 3 levels): 786k geodesic distance evaluations, about 10-20 MFLOP plus 3069 exp/log maps, well under 1 ms of GPU math; extra wall clock per Stage 2 step roughly 5-15% because only the quantizer path is touched, so 3000 epochs stay inside the frozen budget with no extra epochs and no extra runs. One-off: one sparse pass over the training sequences for c_ij and the successor table (minutes, CPU), a 24556-int code cache, and a single deterministic forward pass to measure the curvature scale and the three tau values. Transient memory: three 1023x256 matrices per step.
ideas.coupling_equation: L_ik^(l) = d_P,c( exp_0^c(z_i^(l-1)), exp_0^c(e_lk) )^2 + tau_l*( clip( log q_ik^(l) / log(1/K_l), 0, 1 ) - 1 ), with q_ik^(l) the smoothed successor mass of item i currently assigned to code k at level l.
ideas.coupling_path: One cost function per level: the geodesic distance from the item's residual point in the ball to the code point produces the content term, the successor-code distribution produces the additive margin, and the argmin of their sum decides the SID token the generator later sees; setting tau to 0 removes the behaviour and changes the argmin, replacing d_P by the Euclidean distance removes the curvature and changes the argmin, so neither piece is a decoration.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If content similarity and behaviour-state co-location are largely compatible in the frozen item embeddings, the capped successor-code margin changes level-1 membership for a sizeable minority of items without inflating reconstruction error, the training-only successor prefix-match rate (probability an item shares its level-1 code with at least one training successor) rises over training, the empirical level-1 code-transition entropy H(code_1(next)|code_1(cur)) falls, and the single frozen Stage 3 run exceeds test recall@10 = 0.065. If successor occupancy is uninformative, or reconstruction dominates the margin, the prefix-match rate stays flat and recall stays at baseline: one run falsifies it with no ablation needed.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the quantization step of every RQ level, in the forward assignment of which code each item takes at levels 1, 2 and 3, and therefore inside the straight-through gradient reaching the encoder and the codebooks; the decoder and the reconstruction loss stay exactly as in the baseline.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball distance d_P(u,v) = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-u) +_c v||) with fixed negative curvature K = -c, c derived from the 99th percentile encoder norm so that the farthest training item sits at ball radius 0.9; exp_0 and log_0 maps move the residual accumulator and the codebooks between the tangent space at the origin and the ball.
ideas.key_change: Each RQ level selects its code by argmin over d_P^2(Poincare point of the residual, Poincare point of the code) plus tau_l*(clip(log q / log(1/K),0,1)-1), where q is the count-weighted fraction of the item's training successors currently sitting in that code; tau_l is the level's median nearest-code squared distance and the successor codes come from a detached, at-most-one-epoch-stale cache.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition table, the successor lists, the curvature scale s and the per-level tau_l are all measured from the training split and from the frozen Stage-2 item content embeddings; validation and test interactions never enter. The code cache is written only inside Stage-2 training steps from training batches, is detached (no gradient path) and is dropped before Stage 3. Stage 3 consumes only the frozen integer SID strings, so no validation or test interaction can reach SID construction; the only test-time quantity is the final recall.
ideas.motivation: A generative next-item recommender over SIDs is only as good as the prefix transitions it must predict. In a content-only RQ-VAE, two items that users trade between constantly can land in different level-1 cells, so the generator spends its first tokens re-identifying a behaviour state instead of predicting the next item. The behaviour that matters is not the item's own popularity or its own entropy but WHERE ITS SUCCESSORS LIVE in the code hierarchy: if an item is placed in the cells its successors occupy, the SID sequence becomes a predictable state chain and prefix-level beam search stops discarding the correct branch early.
ideas.novelty: The behaviour term is a predictive distribution over the hierarchy's own alphabet (the current level-l codes of the item's training successors), not a popularity weight, not an entropy-derived radius, not a codebook-update weight and not a per-level curvature control. It enters as a bounded additive margin on an assignment cost whose content term is a Poincare geodesic distance, so cells become geodesic Voronoi regions shifted by behaviour mass. No earlier round computed a successor-code distribution over the codebook alphabet, and none used the cap 'one typical quantization unit' to keep behaviour from overriding content.
ideas.observables: The hard SID strings change for a reported fraction of items relative to the pure curved assignment; the training-only successor prefix-match rate at each level; the empirical level-l code transition entropy and its transfer predictability under a count-based transition model; RQ-VAE reconstruction MSE (must stay near baseline); and Stage 3 test recall@10 as the judgement. Prefix counts, code-usage entropy and collisions are reported as diagnostics only.
risks: Many items may collapse onto hot successor cells; the tau cap, the reconstruction term and the popularity-discounted p_ij mitigate but do not prove this away.; The hyperbolic content term may itself hurt reconstruction, because near the boundary distances are dominated by radius rather than by content direction.; The detached one-epoch-stale code cache can oscillate early in training when codes move fast.; Successor structure may be nearly redundant with content similarity, making the margin a no-op.; The derived tau may be systematically too weak (behaviour ignored) or sit at its cap too often (behaviour overrides fine distinctions).; The Stage 3 generator may not exploit improved prefix self-predictability because its transition head is trained on whatever SIDs it is handed.
ideas.safeguards: Ball clipping so every point stays at radius <= 1-1e-5 and the artanh argument is clipped to 1-1e-6; q smoothed with a uniform pseudocount 1/K_l; margin bounded to [-tau_l, 0] so behaviour can never override a content difference larger than one typical quantization unit; tau measured once at initialisation and then frozen so the feedback loop cannot inflate it; successor code cache detached and at most one epoch stale; items with no training successors, or whose successors fall outside the Stage-2 item set, get margin 0 and fall back to pure curved assignment; any non-finite d2_ik for an item falls back to the Euclidean distance for that item only; the transition table excludes single-interaction users and self-pairs; a final assertion checks sum_k q_ik = 1 and that all SIDs lie within codebook ranges.
ideas.spec_equations: Precompute p_ij as above; derive c from s. Per level: P = exp_0^c(z); C = exp_0^c(e); d2_ik = (2/sqrt(c))*artanh(sqrt(c)*||(-P_i)+_c C_lk||)^2 with the artanh argument clipped to 1-1e-6; n_ik = sum_{j in Succ(i)} p_ij*1[h_l(j)=k]; q_ik = (n_ik+1/K_l)/(n_i+1); s_ik = clip(log q_ik/log(1/K_l),0,1); L_ik = d2_ik + tau_l*(s_ik-1); k* = argmin_k L_ik; forward e* = e_lk*; backward STE: dL/dz += dL/de*, dL/de_lk* += dL/de*; z <- z - e*; h_l(i) = k* after the step. tau_l = median_i(min_k d2_ik) computed once at level initialisation with no gradient. Reconstruction: min ||x_i - dec(sum_l e_lk*)||^2 plus the unchanged baseline terms.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder outputs z_i for a batch, the level codebooks e_l in the tangent space at the origin, the frozen successor CSR block with weights p_ij, the detached code cache h_l, the curvature c and the frozen tau_l. Outputs: per item the three hard code indices (the SID), the straight-through gradients for encoder, codebooks and decoder, and the updated cache entries for the batch.

specification.text: Precompute from training sequences only: c_ij = transitions i->j; w_ij = c_ij/sqrt(1+c_j); p_ij = w_ij/sum_j' w_ij; Succ(i) = top-10 by p_ij (full row allowed). Curvature c = (2*artanh(0.9)/s)^2 with s = 99th percentile of ||enc(x)|| on the first deterministic batch; K = -c, ball radius 1. For level l = 1..3 and batch items i: P_i = exp_0^c(z_i^(l-1)) with z_i^(0)=enc(x_i); C_lk = exp_0^c(e_lk); d2_ik = geodesic distance squared in the ball; n_ik = sum_{j in Succ(i)} p_ij*1[h_l(j)=k]; q_ik = (n_ik + 1/K_l)/(n_i + 1); s_ik = clip(log q_ik/log(1/K_l),0,1); L_ik = d2_ik + tau_l*(s_ik-1); tau_l = median_i min_k d2_ik at level initialisation, detached and frozen; k*(i) = argmin_k L_ik with straight-through selection; z_i^(l) = z_i^(l-1) - e_lk*; decoder loss unchanged; cache h_l updated after the step with the batch's assignments.

ideas.title: Behaviour-state cells: a successor-prefix log-odds margin on a Poincare-distance RQ-VAE assignment

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set A_l(i) = 0 (origin) for all items and levels, giving p_l = p_{l-1} (-) C_l[k_l] and q_{l-1} = q_l (+) C_l[k_l]: exact Mobius residual RQ with geodesic reconstruction and no successor information. Implemented as one boolean that zeroes the frozen anchor table; never run in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full recursion with c=1 Mobius operators and frozen successor anchors at every level plus the exact inverse decode, trained once for the 3000 frozen Stage 2 epochs and evaluated once by the frozen Stage 3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Flat limit c -> 0: exp_0 and log_0 become identity, (+) becomes +, (-) becomes -, d_c becomes L2; the recursion becomes p_l = p_{l-1} - e_l + A_l^Euclid(i), decode x_hat = sum_l e_l - sum_l A_l^Euclid(i), with t_i used unscaled in R^d. Behaviour on, curvature off, selected by one operator-set boolean; never run in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: Training split only: count every ordered consecutive pair (i,v) in training sessions, row-normalise to M, take b = (U S^{1/2}) from a seeded rank-d randomised SVD of M, t_i = tau b_i / max(||b_i||, 1e-8), a_i = exp_0(t_i), A_l(i) = exp_0(0.5^{l-1} t_i). Computed once before Stage 2, stored as a frozen tensor with no gradient, reused every epoch and for the final SID assignment. Popularity is controlled by row normalisation (each source's activity divided out) and absorbed by the leading singular factor.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions from TRAIN-split sessions (consecutive next-item edges), summarised as each item's successor-profile anchor in the Poincare ball.
ideas.cost_estimate: One-off randomised rank-d SVD of a 24556 x 24556 sparse matrix (~123k nnz, seconds to about 1 minute); anchors stored as 24556 x L x d float32 (~9 MB at d=32, L=3). Per step at the frozen scale (24 steps/epoch, batch ~1024, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): L extra Mobius subtractions, about 2L Mobius additions, 2L exp/log on d-vectors plus one exp per level for the decode, i.e. roughly 6L vector ops of size 1024 x 32, well under 1% of the transformer's per-step FLOPs; the K-way argmin distance work is unchanged. Expected wall clock 1.02-1.10x baseline, memory +~10 MB, no extra forward or backward pass, no extra epochs.
ideas.coupling_equation: p_l = (p_{l-1} (-)_c C_l[k_l]) (+)_c A_l(i), with A_l(i) = exp_0^c(rho^{l-1} * tau * b_i / ||b_i||), k_l = argmin_k d_c^c(p_{l-1}, exp_0^c(W_l[k])), and L_rec = mean_i [d_c^c(x_i, x_hat_i)]^2.
ideas.coupling_path: The single pathway is the residual update p_l = (p_{l-1} (-) C_l[k_l]) (+) A_l(i). The behaviour anchor A_l(i) is the operand of the Mobius addition against which the next level's codeword is measured, so the next level's argmin and hence every deeper prefix code depends on the anchor. Setting A_l(i) to the origin removes behaviour and leaves plain curved RQ; replacing Mobius add/subtract, exp/log and d_c by +, -, identity and L2 removes the geometry, including the anchor's action.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the successor frame is the right carrier for prefix refinement, then level-2/3 codes of items inside one behaviour cluster will diverge according to which part of the successor region the item points to, geodesic reconstruction loss will fall at equal L, and Stage 3 test_recall@10 will exceed 0.065 with unchanged codebook size, loss weights and epochs; observed from the single logged test_recall@10 and from the shift of the level-2/3 code histogram under the frame relative to Euclidean framing.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the Stage 2 residual quantizer (encoding recursion p_l and decode recursion q_{l-1}) and in the reconstruction loss; it acts on quantization, not on the recommender backbone.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c=1 Poincare ball: Mobius addition (+) and subtraction (-), exp_0/log_0 maps, and the Poincare distance d_c(x,y) = 2 artanh(||(-x) (+) y||), used both inside the residual recursion and as the reconstruction metric. No trainable curvature, so no curvature sweep exists.
ideas.key_change: Replace the Euclidean residual p_l = p_{l-1} - c_l by p_l = (p_{l-1} (-) C_l[k_l]) (+) A_l(i) in the Poincare ball, with A_l(i) a frozen per-item successor anchor, decode by the exact inverse recursion q_L = 0, q_{l-1} = (q_l (-) A_l(i)) (+) C_l[k_l], and use a geodesic reconstruction loss.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition matrix, its SVD and therefore every anchor A_l(i) are built exclusively from train-split sessions before Stage 2 begins, are frozen with requires_grad=False, and are never recomputed during training or at evaluation. No validation or test interaction and no Stage 3 prefix or successor statistic enters SID construction; validation items only feed the standard reconstruction logging, and an item with no train successor simply gets an origin anchor.
ideas.motivation: In a plain RQ-VAE every prefix level quantizes the same item vector, so coarse prefixes and their refinements all describe the item alone; the generative recommender must learn from Stage 3 data which refinements actually separate an item from its behavioural neighbours. Items inside one behaviour cluster get deep prefix bits spent on directions no successor distinguishes, while the direction toward the successor region, the only one Stage 3 needs, is not privileged. The mechanism forces deeper prefixes to encode the offset of the item from its successor region instead of restating the item.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds changed the codebook (successor-weighted Frechet updates), the curvature scalar (per-level prefix-transition score), or the assignment weight/radius (behaviour-ranked radial assignment, branch-curvature experts). Here the codebook update, the assignment weight and the curvature scalar are untouched: the change is the residual PATH. The residual is carried between frames by Mobius isometries (Mobius subtraction of the chosen codeword, Mobius addition of a frozen behaviour anchor) and the decoder inverts exactly those isometries. Behaviour off reduces the recursion to a plain curved RQ; geometry off reduces it to Euclidean RQ with an additive behaviour offset; neither switch preserves the other.
ideas.observables: (1) Level-2 and level-3 code identity and code histogram for items with non-degenerate anchors, versus Euclidean framing; (2) geodesic reconstruction loss per level, flat after level 1 meaning the frame does nothing; (3) prefix-to-successor transfer predictability over shared-prefix groups (diagnostic only, never a gate); (4) frame sensitivity: number of items whose nearest codeword changes when the anchor is removed at inference; (5) Stage 3 test_recall@10 against the 0.065 bar.
risks: Sparse tail: most items have fewer than two train successors, so their anchor is near-origin and the mechanism degenerates to plain curved RQ exactly where SIDs are least used; the head may carry the whole gain.; SVD factors of the transition matrix are popularity-driven, so the anchor may encode popularity rather than a behaviour direction.; Mobius recursion drift: accumulated frame offsets can push p_l toward the ball boundary where artanh gradients saturate and the straight-through code choice is unstable.; The geodesic reconstruction loss replaces the baseline squared Euclidean loss, so a recall change could be attributed to the loss rather than to the frame coupling; a single run cannot separate these, the coupling's own evidence being the two switches.; The randomised SVD rank is fixed to the encoder width d rather than chosen by validation, which is a hidden design choice.; If the encoder collapses to near-origin points (common in RQ-VAE), exp/log are almost linear, curvature barely acts, and the both-on arm may behave like the Euclidean one.
ideas.safeguards: Clip every tangent norm to R=atanh(0.9) before exp_0 so ball points stay at radius <= 0.9 and artanh is never evaluated at 1; clamp the Mobius-addition denominator to >= 1e-8 and clamp ||(-x)(+)y|| to <= 1-1e-7 before artanh; use the stable Mobius form with the (1+2<x,y>+||x||^2||y||^2) denominator and per-batch norm shifting where available; define exp_0(0)=0 and log_0(0)=0 by convention; anchor rows of items with no train successor are exactly zero so they fall back to plain curved RQ; the whole anchor tensor is a frozen buffer built with a fixed seed and a deterministic SVD sign convention so the run is reproducible; rho=0.5 and tau=atanh(0.5) are documented defaults never swept and c=1 is fixed so there is no curvature search; one step-0 check sets codes to the exact per-level residuals and verifies d_c(x_i, x_hat_i) < 1e-3, validating the decode inversion before any training.
ideas.spec_equations: c=1; R=atanh(0.9)=1.4722; tau=atanh(0.5)=0.5493; rho=0.5. exp_0(v)=tanh(||v||) v/||v|| (0 at v=0); log_0(x)=artanh(||x||) x/||x||; for c=1, x(+)y = ((1+2<x,y>+||y||^2) x + (1-||x||^2) y)/(1+2<x,y>+||x||^2||y||^2); d_c(x,y)=2 artanh(||(-x)(+)y||). Precompute: M = row-normalised train transitions; [U,S,~] = rsvd(M,d); b = U S^{1/2}; sign-fix columns; t_i = tau b_i/max(||b_i||,1e-8) if item i has a successor else 0; A_l(i)=exp_0(rho^{l-1} t_i). Encode: z=E(i); z = clip_norm(z,R); x=exp_0(z); p=x; for l=1..L: dist_k = d_c(p, exp_0(W_l[k])) for k=1..K; k_l = argmin; p = (p (-) exp_0(W_l[k_l])) (+) A_l(i). Decode: q=0; for l=L..1: q = (q (-) A_l(i)) (+) exp_0(W_l[k_l]); x_hat=q. Loss: L = mean_i d_c(x_i,x_hat_i)^2 + beta_cm * mean_{i,l} ||log_0(p_{l-1}) - W_l[k_l]||^2 + baseline usage term, with beta_cm and the usage weight exactly as the baseline config (no new weights), straight-through to codebooks and encoder. SID_i = (k_1..k_L) from the trained recursion.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder tangents z_i (batch x d), codebook tangent tables W_l (K x d), frozen anchor tangents t_i (num_items x d), booleans use_behaviour and use_curvature, curvature c=1. Outputs: chosen code tuple (k_1..k_L) per item, reconstructed ball point x_hat_i, scalar geodesic reconstruction loss and its gradient with respect to the encoder output and to W_l.

specification.text: Curvature fixed at c=1 (unit Poincare ball, documented default, never tuned). Encoder output z_i in R^d, clipped to ||z_i|| <= R = atanh(0.9) = 1.4722, point x_i = exp_0(z_i) = tanh(||z_i||) z_i/||z_i||. Codebooks stored as tangent tables W_l in R^{K x d}, points C_l = exp_0(W_l); K and L are exactly the frozen baseline config values. BEHAVIOUR ANCHOR, computed ONCE before Stage 2 and frozen: build the row-normalised directed transition matrix M from TRAIN-split session transitions only, M[i,v] = count(i->v)/sum_v count(i->v); take a rank-d randomised SVD M ~ U S V^T with fixed RNG seed and a fixed sign convention (flip each left-singular column so its largest-magnitude entry is positive); item factor b_i = (U S^{1/2})_i; anchor tangent t_i = tau * b_i / max(||b_i||, eps) with tau = atanh(0.5) = 0.5493 (documented mid-ball default) and t_i = 0 when item i has no train successor; a_i = exp_0(t_i); store A_l(i) = exp_0(0.5^{l-1} t_i) for l = 1..L (rho = 0.5 is a documented geometric contraction so the accumulated frame offset sum_l rho^{l-1} < 2 stays bounded; level 1 carries the full successor offset, finer levels the shrunken remainder). ENCODE: p_0 = x_i; for l = 1..L: k_l = argmin_k d_c(p_{l-1}, C_l[k]); p_l = (p_{l-1} (-) C_l[k_l]) (+) A_l(i), where x (-) y = x (+) (-y) and (+) is Mobius addition. DECODE: q_L = 0; for l = L..1: q_{l-1} = (q_l (-) A_l(i)) (+) C_l[k_l]; x_hat_i = q_0; the inversion is exact because each encoding step is an isometry. LOSS: L_rec = mean_i d_c(x_i, x_hat_i)^2 with d_c(x,y) = 2 artanh(||(-x) (+) y||); the baseline's commitment and codebook-usage terms keep their baseline weights, the commitment term evaluated on log_0(p_{l-1}) against W_l[k_l]. Straight-through code selection as in the baseline. SID = (k_1,...,k_L) from the same recursion at the end of training.

ideas.title: Successor-framed residual quantization: every RQ level re-expresses the residual in a frozen behaviour anchor frame through Mobius isometries, so the whole SID prefix hierarchy is quantized relative to where the item's train-split successors live

objective: Improve the item semantic IDs of a generative recommender: a training-only behaviour signal must guide the whole SID prefix hierarchy in a hyperbolic RQ-VAE, and the result must raise the Stage 3 test recall above 0.065.
